illustration.caption: Ward Four · an advance, still conditional
illustration.description: Quill rests two fingertips on a plain chip on his own side of the stall counter; his other hand stays beside the untouched bowl. No payment changes hands.

rules.reason: Only an actually successful negotiation permits the forward-but-untransferred chip. Acceptance, payment and intact delivery remain separate.

illustration.caption: Ward Four · the offer stays at fifty
illustration.description: Quill holds a guarded posture beside the bowl; the plain chip stays back on his side of the counter. His visible hand and folded arm remain separate, with no transfer.

rules.reason: A failed negotiation permits the guarded posture and retained chip. It depicts no new refusal of the entire job, punishment or completed payment.

illustration.caption: Helion · before a name goes on the request
illustration.description: Edda pauses with a pencil above a blank unsigned request sheet, her other hand open beside it. The closed ledger stays separate under the archive lamp.

rules.reason: The inspected movement question permits a paused pencil, not an accepted signature. No fee, source, eligibility for a badge method or permission is implied.

illustration.caption: Helion · the copy and its limits
illustration.description: Edda rests one hand on her closed ledger and the other beside a separate folded copy. The pencil is set down; no signature, public name, seal or handover is shown.

rules.reason: An actual scoped extraction permits separate record/copy props. It portrays no paid advance, authenticated issuing key, signature, transfer of custody or consent to naming.

illustration.caption: Ward Four · room for a private question
illustration.description: Mara regards the unseen visitor from beside the rainy clinic window. Her own cup and closed envelope remain on her side of the table, with the empty visitor chair separate.

rules.reason: An acknowledged personal account permits a closer listening composition. Distance, deflection and unsupported visits retain original art; no forgiveness, treatment, public permission or promised future is depicted.
